feed.title: UK News - The latest headlines from the UK | Sky News

articles.title: Drivers who killed mother and young daughter as they raced are jailed
articles.summary: Two strangers who killed a mother and her four-year-old daughter as they raced their high-performance cars along a city centre road have been jailed for 16 and 12 years.

articles.title: Will Harry Kane win tonight's Ballon d'Or?
articles.summary: Tonight's Ballon d'Or is one of the most anticipated in years, with Harry Kane the favourite to be named the world's best men's footballer.

articles.title: London's Oxford Street pedestrianised in 'truly momentous occasion for capital'
articles.summary: London's Oxford Street is now traffic-free, with mayor Sadiq Khan hailing it "a truly momentous occasion for the capital".

articles.title: Senior doctors to strike for two days in November
articles.summary: Senior doctors in England plan to go on strike for two days in November over pay, the British Medical Association (BMA) has said.

articles.title: Two men killed in multi-vehicle crash
articles.summary: Two men have died in a multi-vehicle collision in West Lothian.

articles.title: Second person charged in connection with shooting of police officer in Nottingham
articles.summary: A second person has been charged in connection with the shooting of a police officer in Nottingham city centre on 18 October.

articles.title: Met Office issues new weather warning for wind - as two men killed by falling trees
articles.summary: The Met Office has issued a new wind weather warning after Storm Boelo pummelled the UK with gusts of up to 84mph, flooded streets and caused power cuts to 800,000 homes.

articles.title: Boy, 17, arrested after teenager dies in crash following police chase
articles.summary: A teenage boy has been arrested after a boy died in a crash following a police pursuit.

articles.title: Power surge at major UK airport delays hundreds of flights
articles.summary: A power surge at Stansted Airport has caused hundreds of flights to be delayed.

articles.title: Police to allow some offenders to breach curfews without arrest
articles.summary: The Metropolitan Police is reducing enforcement of offenders who breach their tag conditions amid resourcing pressures and following early prisoner release.
